title: Competency credential — what a person demonstrated, and who stood behind it
description: The portable attestation the individual OWNS. It serialises into a W3C Verifiable Credential 2.0 with an Open Badges 3.0 achievement, and this schema governs the claim payload that becomes the credentialSubject. Verification is a signature check against a signed issuer trust registry distributed as a file — no ledger, no network, no call to the issuer. A credential attests competence and NEVER authority: see authorization.schema.json, and decision 6 in CLAUDE.md. Held in dual custody, because ISO/IEC 17025 §6.2 requires the laboratory to hold competence records for audit while the individual needs portability; both hold a true copy and neither can erase the other's.

id.description: Stable identifier for this credential. A UUID rather than a sequence: issuance happens offline and in parallel across organizations that cannot coordinate a counter.

subject.description: The person who holds this. Minimal PII by design — a DID, not a name, birthdate or national ID. A holder may bind a display name locally; nothing requires it to travel.

kind.description: Recorded on the credential itself, not merely resolvable from the taxonomy. A reader years later must be able to tell what KIND of claim this is — explanation, performance, or defended judgement — without the corpus in hand.

assessedAtScope.description: Every level is assessed at element scope, so 'CM-03-048 at L2' means that element was assessed and not that some cluster containing it was. Fixed as a const because a credential's meaning cannot be renegotiated after issue; an overlay making the opposite trade must say so on its own credentials rather than reusing this schema.

expiresOn.description: Recertification date, from the level default unless the element overrides it. An expired credential is not a false one: it remains true that the competence was demonstrated on the date it was demonstrated. Verifiers decide what weight to give currency.

provenanceTier.description: VISIBLE, always. This is how the entry-barrier principle and the rigor principle coexist: nothing is blocked, and the difference is legible rather than hidden. A hiring manager sees not only what was demonstrated but who stood behind it. Suppressing this field in a renderer defeats the design.

assessment.description: How it was earned, recorded so a reader need not assume.

archetypes.description: Which item shapes were served. Archetype IDs are append-only precisely so this stays resolvable after an archetype is retired.

attemptRef.description: Pointer into the attempt ledger. What makes 'one attempt, no retakes' mean anything for a challenge exam.

experienceHours.description: Hours claimed against this element. Under decision 37 one activity credits every element it genuinely exercises, so this figure is not exclusive to this credential and must not be summed across a wallet as though it were.

evidence.description: Archived, hashed artifacts. Hashing is what lets any credential be independently re-reviewed years later — including by someone challenging it.

signers.description: Who attested. NO SELF-SIGNOFF EVER: the validator rejects a credential whose subject appears here. Structural, not procedural — a rule enforced only by policy is a rule that fails under pressure.

heldLevel.description: The level this signer held IN THIS ELEMENT at signing time. Null is legitimate at L1 and L2, where a witness attests only that they saw the work.

organization.description: Recorded so cross-organizational signing at L5 is checkable, and so reciprocal-review patterns can be detected.

trustRegistryEntry.description: Key into the signed issuer trust registry. Verification resolves the issuer here, offline, from a distributed file — never by contacting the issuer.

portable.description: Competency credentials travel with the person. Stated explicitly and redundantly so that the contrast with an authorization is visible in the data itself, not only in documentation — see authorization.schema.json, where the same field is const false.

status.description: Revocation exists for fraud and for demonstrable assessment failure. It does NOT exist for an employer who has fallen out with the holder: a competency credential records something that happened, and an organization cannot un-happen it.

cryptosuite.description: ECDSA P-256, not Ed25519. Ed25519 is the VC ecosystem default and the better curve by most engineering measures, but FIPS 140-3 validation is required for the DoD deployments this must support and P-256 (FIPS 186-5) is the approved choice. Expensive to reverse: every credential already issued is signed with the suite in force at the time.

did.description: A decentralized identifier. The method is deliberately not fixed here — the Personal edition must work with no server and no registrar, so a purely cryptographic method has to remain viable.
